title: Hybrid Perturbation on 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 Dual-Band IR Filter
scientific_hypothesis: Applying wider perturbation bounds to the front half of the stack (layers 1-12) while restricting the back half (layers 13-22) to narrow local adjustments will improve the dual-band transmittance score without degrading stopband rejection, compared to uniform perturbation across all layers.
design_principle: In multilayer interference filters, the front layers primarily control impedance matching and overall transmission, while the back layers fine-tune spectral positioning. Asymmetric perturbation allows global exploration where it matters most while preventing phase disruption in the terminating layers.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 layers total, alternating high/low index)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers
Perturbation bounds: layers 1-12 at ±8% global exploration, layers 13-22 at ±5% with ±3 nm maximum displacement cap from iteration 08 seed
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: All layers must be depositable by conventional PVD or CVD methods
Total layer count fixed at 22 (within 24-layer limit)
Thicknesses should remain in practical deposition range (50-1000 nm)
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength; deviating from quarter-wave can create transmission windows
Recalled knowledge: ZnS has high refractive index (~2.2-2.4) in mid-IR and is transparent through 5 μm
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has low refractive index (~1.3-1.4) and reasonable transmission in 4-5 μm range though absorption increases beyond 4 μm
Recalled knowledge: Daimon-20 dataset provides CaF2 substrate optical constants in 3-5 μm range
Recalled knowledge: Front layers in a stack affect impedance matching more than back layers, which primarily tune phase
expected_advantages: Hybrid perturbation should find better local optima than uniform bounds
Restricting back layers prevents destructive interference pattern shifts
Front layer exploration can improve overall transmission efficiency
Builds on iteration 08 best result (target score 0.698) as seed
known_risks: MgF2 absorption coefficient at 4-5 μm is uncertain from memory; actual k values may reduce transmission more than expected
Daimon-20 dataset selection was required because generic CaF2 name matched 4 datasets equally; this specific dataset may not match all prior iteration assumptions
The ±3 nm cap on layers 13-22 may be too restrictive if iteration 08 seed is not near optimum
ZnS stress and adhesion properties not verified; may affect manufacturability
What would settle this: Look up measured n/k data for MgF2 and ZnS at 4-5 μm from handbook or vendor data sheets
